mission.cluster: B — global task identity / lifecycle / durable state

adaptation: TypeScript -> ESM JavaScript. §35 of the donor's candidate gate (TASK_LIFECYCLE, TASK_TRANSITIONS, the forward/backward event tables, advanceLifecycle, CandidateRecord/CandidateRecordFor and candidateIdFor) is carried over with identical rules.

Only §35 is ported here. §36 of the same donor file (the seven-plus-four Guardian checklist) is a gate rather than a lifecycle and lives in the sibling `audit-ledger` module. The split is by mission cluster, not by donor file, and both halves cite the same donor.

The donor's `contentHashOf` (src/shared/workbook.ts) is inlined as a private helper instead of importing workbook.ts: it is exactly `sha256hex(utf8(text))`, and pulling in workbook.ts would drag a 25 KB workbook module into a lifecycle primitive.

`CandidateRecord.guardian` is carried as an opaque value here. The donor types it as `GuardianVerdict`; that shape is owned by `audit-ledger`, so this module does not re-declare it and does not validate it.
The donor's `new Date(0).toISOString()` default for `created_at` is kept deliberately: a record built without an injected clock stays deterministic instead of silently reading the wall clock.

Structural validation (`TaskLifecycleError`) and copy-on-construct for the record's lists were added so a malformed step or a caller-mutated array cannot silently corrupt a record. No transition rule was added, removed or relaxed.
knownDifferences: No task runtime, no store, no event bus and no persistence: the module is pure and the durable record is the caller's to store.

The donor's broader task vocabulary (TaskStatus queued/running/waiting/paused/cancelled/completed/failed, BossTask, task-presentation's UserTaskState projection) is NOT migrated here. It is entangled with the Boss provider/council runtime and is explicitly out of this module's boundary.
No secret scanning, no requirement graph, no review pipeline: §36's external observations are supplied by the caller to `audit-ledger`.
Nothing in this module reads a clock, a filesystem or an environment variable.

vectors: TASK_LIFECYCLE is exactly RUNNING, IMPLEMENTED, VERIFYING, REVIEWING, CANDIDATE, ACCEPTED in that order
every state's edge set is exactly its forward target plus its one-step repair target, so no jump is expressible
ACCEPTED is terminal: no event leaves it and its allowed set is empty
a refused event returns accepted=false with the state unchanged, the allowed set and a reason naming the full lifecycle
REPAIR moves exactly one state back and is labelled as a repair
the forward move lands on the next DECLARED state, not on an event-named target
CANDIDATE sets awaiting_release_permission=true; only ACCEPTED clears it
candidateIdFor sorts the requirements, joins with NUL and truncates SHA-256 to 16 hex characters (pinned vector cand-6f6181a33382dced)
a record built without a clock is byte-identical across calls and uses the Unix epoch
unknown states and unknown events are refused rather than guessed

PARITY: the §35 lifecycle order and edge tables
advanceLifecycle's forward and one-step repair results and reason strings
candidateRecordFor's awaiting_release_permission rule and epoch default
PORT_ADAPTATION: contentHashOf inlined instead of importing workbook.ts
guardian carried as an opaque value owned by the audit-ledger module
structural validation and copy-on-construct added around the ported rules
UTOPIA_EXTENSION: TERMINAL_LIFECYCLE_STATES, isLifecycleState and isLifecycleEvent are convenience queries derived from the donor's own tables; they add no transition and no rule.
DEFERRED: §36 Guardian checklist (landed in the sibling audit-ledger module)
any task store, scheduler or provider runtime
